title: When the Inheritance Burns
premise: When Ada Sterling, the coroner of Hollow Creek, is ordered to exhume the town's founder for a land dispute, she finds the coffin empty—and a fresh body buried beneath it. The corpse belongs to a man reported dead thirty years ago on the same night the founder's heir vanished, and the statute of limitations on the original crimes expires in six weeks. As Ada digs through sealed records and the town's carefully curated memory, she discovers her own late mother helped bury the truth, forcing her to choose between belonging in Hollow Creek and exposing what it was built on. In the end, Ada confronts the founder's still-living daughter—the true architect of both deaths—and chooses exile over silence, publishing the truth as the statute clock runs out.
about_author: Sable Hartwell spent a decade as a rural journalist covering small-town courtrooms before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries about communities that protect their own secrets at any cost.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Ada Sterling's POV. A quiet autumn morning in the Hollow Creek morgue establishes Ada's intimate knowledge of the town's dead and her deliberate invisibility among the living. The emotional beat is melancholy competence—she belongs to the dead more than the living.

chapters.title: The Order
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A court order arrives: exhumation of founder Elias Marsh, whose remains are needed to settle an inheritance dispute between his estranged granddaughters. Town council members react with uncharacteristic alarm. Beat: first tremor of wrongness beneath civic politeness.

chapters.title: Dirt That Should Be Still
chapters.summary: Ada's POV at the cemetery. The coffin comes up light; inside, no Elias Marsh—only river stones and a rotted tarp. Beneath the vault, a second, newer grave holds a man's body. Beat: shock hardening into professional resolve.

chapters.title: A Face from 1994
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Dental records identify the hidden body as Daniel Voss, declared drowned thirty years ago—the night Elias Marsh supposedly died and his heir, Ruthie, disappeared. Beat: dread as two old cases collapse into one.

chapters.title: The Alibi Book
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ada and retired sheriff Walt Denner. Walt recalls the sealed 1994 investigation; every prominent family had an alibi, too neat, all signed by the same notary. Beat: suspicion that the alibis were manufactured together.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Clearing her late mother's attic, Ada finds a key and a note in her mother's handwriting: 'If they ever open the ground, leave.' Beat: betrayal—the person she trusted most was complicit.

chapters.title: The Granddaughters
chapters.summary: Ada's POV interviewing Claire and June Marsh, the disputing heirs. Claire wants the exhumation stopped; June pushed for it. Both lie about their whereabouts last month. Beat: Ada realizes someone modern wanted that grave opened.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Walt's POV. Flashback chapter to 1994: young Walt was ordered off the Voss drowning case by the then-sheriff, who retired rich soon after. Beat: guilt and the corrosion of institutional power.

chapters.title: The Notary's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following her mother's key to a bank box, Ada finds the notary ledger showing eleven alibi affidavits signed within one hour, plus a deed transferring Marsh land to shell companies. Beat: the conspiracy had a paper spine.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her office is searched; the ledger copy she left there is gone. A threatening note quotes her mother's attic note verbatim. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance—she can't be invisible anymore.

chapters.title: Ruthie
chapters.summary: Claire's POV. Claire confesses she received anonymous letters claiming 'Ruthie' was alive—that Elias's vanished heir never died, and the body under the coffin proves who did. Beat: the missing girl becomes the story's beating heart.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man Who Walked
chapters.summary: Walt's POV. Walt tracks a witness who saw Daniel Voss alive three days after his 'drowning,' boarding a bus with a woman matching Ruthie's description. Beat: hope—the victims may have fled together.

chapters.title: Midnight Reburial
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Someone attempts to rebury the vault overnight; Ada catches them—June Marsh, terrified, holding her grandmother's letters. June reveals the family knew Elias's coffin was empty all along. Beat: alliance forming across old bloodlines.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Legal counsel confirms: accessory liability for the 1994 cover-up expires in five weeks. Whoever orchestrated everything must destroy evidence—or witnesses—before then. Beat: ticking-clock pressure formalized.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek Turns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The town fractures: council moves to suspend Ada, her mother's complicity leaks, and old friends cross the street to avoid her. Beat: the cost of belonging—Ada loses the community she stayed invisible to keep.

chapters.title: The Second Body's Secret
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Forensics show Daniel Voss died recently—not thirty years ago. He returned to Hollow Creek weeks back, met someone, and was killed to keep him silent forever. Beat: the past reached out and was strangled.

chapters.title: Letters from Ruthie
chapters.summary: June's POV. June shares decades of unsigned letters postmarked from coastal towns—Ruthie alive, hiding, protected by whoever controlled the money. The final letter, three months old, says Daniel found her. Beat: grief and urgency collide.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Evidence converges on Marion Voss—Daniel's sister, the town's beloved historical society president, who married into the Marsh fortune and has quietly run Hollow Creek for thirty years. Beat: the horror of realizing the kindest face built the cage.

chapters.title: Confession at the Founders' Hall
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax part one. Ada lures Marion to Founders' Hall with the recovered ledger. Marion admits staging the 1994 deaths to seize the estate, hunting down Daniel when he resurfaced. Beat: chilling calm of corrupted power explaining itself.

chapters.title: Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: Walt and Ada POV, climax part two. Marion sets fire to the hall's archive to burn the last records; Ada saves the ledger and nearly dies; Walt arrests Marion as Ruthie's location surfaces from a scorched envelope. Beat: sacrifice, chaos, and the truth surviving flame.

chapters.title: The Woman on the Coast
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada travels to meet Ruthie Marsh, living quietly under another name. Ruthie confirms everything but asks not to be exposed. Beat: compassion versus duty—Ada understands why people vanish from Hollow Creek.

chapters.title: When the Inheritance Burns
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, resolution. Ada publishes the full account, naming names including her mother's, and resigns as coroner. Ruthie stays hidden; Marion awaits trial; Ada leaves town, finally visible on her own terms. Beat: bittersweet freedom—belonging traded for identity.
